title: Neil Armstrong's 'truth's protective layers' speech
summary: Jesse Michels tells of Neil Armstrong's 'truth's protective layers' speech, about 1980s (as stated) at United States (no place named), and frames it as the host. As told, not a fact.

plain: Neil Armstrong, the astronaut who walked on the Moon, once gave a speech that some read as a coded hint about hidden knowledge. A podcast host, Jesse Michels, quotes it: "There are great ideas undiscovered. Breakthroughs available to those who can remove one of truth's protective layers." Michels first remembered it as a 1980s speech at a medal ceremony, but in a later episode he places it at the White House in 1994. Another podcast host, Joe Rogan, says it was given 25 years after the moon landing, to the brightest high school students. Those who tell it hear Armstrong hinting that important truths are still being kept from the public.
